gaps: AS-04 (soft delete is recoverable by an operator) can only be verified by inspecting the MongoDB document directly — TC-33/TC-34 assert the surviving deleted_at, but the contract exposes no restore endpoint to test recovery end to end.

BR-07's concurrency guarantee (the unique index deciding a race between two simultaneous registrations of the same email) is not covered by a test case, because the runner issues requests sequentially; TC-02 covers only the sequential 409 path.

BR-08's timing-equivalence half (the dummy bcrypt compare making unknown-email and wrong-password indistinguishable in response time) is not asserted — TC-08 verifies only that the status and body are identical, since wall-clock timing is too noisy for a deterministic assertion.
No frontend artifacts were provided, so no UI-level tests exist for the React client described in the diagram (token storage, list rendering, compose box).

No Product Manager artifact was provided — personas, goals, success metrics, and prioritisation rationale are unavailable. The user guide's persona section is derived solely from the 'Note owner' actor in the architecture diagram.
No UI/UX artifact was provided — there are no wireframes, user flows, screen states, or interface copy to document.

No Frontend artifact was provided — the React SPA appears in the architecture diagram but no code, components, routing, or token-storage strategy exists. The user guide therefore documents the product at the API level only.

No deployment or operations artifact was provided — hosting, TLS termination, CORS, secret management, logging, health checks, backups, and migrations are undocumented. Notably, utils/token.js falls back to the hardcoded string 'pact-local-development-secret' when JWT_SECRET is unset, and unlike MONGO_URL its absence does not fail startup.
No artifact specifies rate limiting or login throttling, so the API reference cannot document any protection against credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts.

AS-04 (soft delete is recoverable by an operator) has no supporting endpoint — recovery is database-level only, so neither the spec nor the guide can describe a restore path, and QA cannot verify recovery end to end.

QA reported that BR-07's concurrency guarantee (the unique index deciding a race between two simultaneous registrations of the same email) is untested, because the runner issues requests sequentially; only the sequential 409 path (TC-02) is covered.

QA reported that BR-08's timing-equivalence half (the dummy bcrypt compare) is not asserted — TC-08 verifies only that status and body are identical, as wall-clock timing is too noisy for a deterministic assertion.

The architecture contract reports completeness_score 0.62, and the two load-bearing assumptions AS-01 (auth model, confidence 0.55) and AS-04 (soft delete, confidence 0.45) are unconfirmed by the brief — if either is wrong, the auth model or the delete semantics documented here change.
